video_title: Caitlin Clark & Kelsey Mitchell: The Greatest Backcourt in WNBA History? + Full Playoff Preview

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell having historic statistical seasons
quotes.excerpt: Caitlin is having the greatest statistical season ever by a point guard in this league
quotes.quote: You could absolutely make an argument that Caitlin is having the greatest statistical season ever by a point guard in this league and Kelsey is having the greatest statistical season ever by a shooting guard in this league.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Lynx are the team to beat in the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: The basketball gods, oh Minnesota one.
quotes.quote: The basketball gods, oh Minnesota one. And so, I usually feel like the universe usually makes those things right at some point.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: Ty Harris could be in line for an Aliyah Boston sponsorship
quotes.excerpt: Ty Harris may now have an Aliyah Boston sponsorship coming after her moment on the podium
quotes.quote: Just like Ty Harris may now have an Aliyah Boston sponsorship coming after her moment on the podium with Caitlin Clark, I am very happy to have a Waterloo sponsorship should they decide. I love these different flavors and Apple Pie Alamode is delicious, so you're welcome.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: The WNBA playoff schedule and the FIBA break
quotes.excerpt: The FIBA break is upon us, that begins September 4th.
quotes.quote: The FIBA break is upon us, that begins September 4th. And the more and more I think about it by the way guys, that's a 16-day window. It's a break for the WNBA, but obviously those stars are playing that are playing in FIBA. That's wild.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Robinson
quotes.summary_phrase: WNBA teams face momentum challenges during the FIBA break
quotes.excerpt: The momentum for so many teams are just, they don't want that break.
quotes.quote: The momentum for so many teams are just, they don't want that break. Some teams may want that break, but especially when you have an All-Star break, quote-unquote, that's not really a break. This is a gap of time that can either get people off of their game or, you know, some teams like I think of the Mystics who has one player that's going to be on the FIBA team, this is a time where they can regroup, iron out anything that they need to before the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: WNBA schedule changes impact team rhythm and playoff preparation
quotes.excerpt: If this was the NBA, people would have been talking about it all.
quotes.quote: If this was the NBA, people would have been talking about it all. When the schedule came out immediately like, what? With four games left in the season, you're going to take a two-week break? Like, huh? And this used to not be the way it was, and I believe it will not be the case moving forward. I think FIBA is sliding the timing of their tournament in years to come, but it used to be that the W would finish the finals and then you'd have the FIBA tournament.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: Parity defines the current WNBA playoff race
quotes.excerpt: Parity, I think is the one word I would use to describe it.
quotes.quote: Parity, I think is the one word I would use to describe it. I think there's a clear top team, Minnesota. They clearly have been the best team all season. But then if you look, and even including Golden State, but if you look at the rest of the teams, it's astonishing how few, four games separate two through eight. It's crazy. Three games separate three through eight. Two and a half games separate four through eight. We have some wild tiebreaker scenarios.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: Nalyssa Smith's injury is a major concern for the Aces
quotes.excerpt: The thing I'm most intrigued about right now team-wise is the Aces with the Nalyssa Smith injury.
quotes.quote: The thing I'm most intrigued about right now team-wise is the Aces with the Nalyssa Smith injury. Because Nalyssa Smith is not the first best player, obviously on their team. She's not the second best player on the team. She's not the third best player on the team, obviously. She's really important to their team. And Becky Hammon will tell you, she changed their season last year acquiring her. She also this year has been playing really well. She got herself in tip-top shape, reminding me of what I felt watching her at Baylor, especially her junior year there, and not having her just becomes a spacing problem for them in their starting five.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Robinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Atlanta Dream's star players and their inconsistent performance
quotes.excerpt: They have All-Stars in Ryan Howard, Allie Shagrey, Angel Reese. Have they all gone off at the same time?
quotes.quote: They have All-Stars in Ryan Howard, Allie Shagrey, Angel Reese. Have they all gone off at the same time? Not always. Sometimes it's Ryan Howard's night, sometimes it's Allie Shagrey, then it's Angel Reese. If they can all be an X-factor together, that is what's going to get them over the edge.

quotes.speaker: Ryan Ruocco
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Canada is the X-factor for the Atlanta Dream
quotes.quote: For me, it's Jordan Canada. And my reasoning is, especially in the matchup with Indiana, she has been statistically the most effective defender on Kaitlyn Clark. She is a hounding perimeter defender. She also allows less of a defensive load on Ryan Howard, too, because she, like Ryan, is a premier perimeter defender. And she's been very effective on offense in getting them out running, which is what they want to do. She's a fast player. She has experience, she's won multiple championships in Seattle.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: The depth of elite guard talent in the WNBA playoffs
quotes.excerpt: on any given night, you could see history from Paige, from Kelsey, from Caitlin, from Olivia Miles
quotes.quote: Now we have all these incredible guards where you go into the playoffs and you are like, on any given night, you could see history from Paige, from Kelsey, from Caitlin, from Olivia Miles. That is just to name a few. From the most underrated player in the history of the league, Caitlin McBryde. There is just incredible guard talent to go with the overall historic excellence of A'ja, and Stewie, and Fee. I am excited for that. Like you said, when it matters most.
